**My thinking as this farmer:**

I've been at this for 4 years, so I know the basics but I'm not going to try anything too experimental. Quzhou is wheat-maize country — that's what everyone around me grows and it's what the land is suited for. I'll keep the rotation going on most of my 200 mu. Wheat goes in October after the maize comes off, maize goes in June after wheat. That's 150 mu locked into that cycle.

The other 50 mu I split between cabbage and stevia. Stevia is a good cash earner and doesn't need much from me once it's established — I keep about 20 mu on it. Cabbage I grow in autumn on 30 mu; the timing works around my wheat planting and the market price is decent in late October through December.

For seeds, I use hybrid maize — everyone does, the yields are just better. For wheat I buy the improved variety the seed station recommends. For cabbage I go with improved seed too. Stevia I use transplanted seedlings from cuttings I kept from last year's plot.

Fertilizer — I apply roughly what the agricultural station pamphlet says. I probably use a bit more nitrogen than I should on wheat because my neighbor says it helps with yield and I don't want to fall short. I have well irrigation so I use it at the critical stages: wheat gets water at sowing, winter recharge, jointing, and grain fill. Maize gets water at emergence, tasseling, and grain fill.

Pesticides: mostly herbicide early, then fungicide or aphid spray for wheat. Cabbage needs more attention — caterpillars and aphids.

I'll use rotary tillage before wheat planting and go no-tillage on maize since it's seeded directly into the wheat stubble. That saves me labor and fuel.
